title: That Night
description:
It rained. The sound of it against the window made the small room feel even smaller.

It had been a hard day for both of them. Daeun brought a bottle of soju and some convenience-store snacks. She hadn't packed an umbrella — the ends of her hair were wet — and when {name} handed her a towel, she smiled.
"Thanks. ...For some reason, I didn't want to go straight home tonight."

Under the low light, the soju glasses passed back and forth a couple of times. They laughed, then talked less — and at some point only the rain was left.

Daeun looked at {name} for a long moment. Instead of her usual shyness, tonight she didn't look away. Neither did he.
Between two people in their thirties, there was a distance that no longer needed explaining. And little by little, it closed.

Her fingertips touched the back of his hand. He'd expected them cold; they were warm. And trembling, just slightly.
"...Minjun." Her voice was lower than usual.

And on that word, Daeun reached over and turned off the light.

choices.text: Take that trembling hand in his.
choices.result_text:
{name} took that trembling hand in his. In the dark, Daeun's breath came closer.
The rain filled the room — and the rest of that night belonged to the two of them alone.

Morning. He woke as a grey light came through the window. Two people, in the narrow bed.
Daeun was still asleep, her head on his arm. A face that hadn't turned once all night.
Her glasses lay where she'd taken them off, by the pillow. That one small thing said it plainly: this was no longer a room for one.

Gangnam, three billion — that morning, at least, they were very far away.
For a man whose only possession was this one room — today, that was enough.

choices.text: "...Just stay next to me tonight." (Falls asleep holding her)
choices.result_text:
{name} held her hand, but pulled the blanket up over her damp shoulders.
"...Let's just stay like this tonight."
Daeun looked startled for a second, then smiled quietly. "...You really are tender in the strangest places, Minjun."

They lay side by side in the narrow bed and listened to the rain against the window. Daeun's breathing slowed, and before long she was asleep on his shoulder.
Being two people who didn't have to hurry — somehow that ran deeper.

Love in your thirties — it held firmer precisely because it wasn't in a rush.

title: The Last Cup
description:
Five years are almost up.

An evening cafe. Across the table, Daeun worried at the paper sleeve around her cold coffee. The same figures had sat on {name}'s phone for days: the price of a ring, the cash he had left, the distance still separating him from Gangnam.

"Minjun, why are you so quiet tonight?"

Instead of answering, {name} slipped a hand into his pocket, then pulled it back out. His fingertips had caught the corner of a small box. Daeun waited with no idea what was there.

choices.text: Turn the phone face down. Ask where she wants to be next year.
choices.result_text:
"Daeun, where do you want to be this time next year?"

She thought for a moment, then let go of the paper sleeve. "Anywhere. Somewhere I open the door and find your shoes beside mine."

She said it like a joke, but her eyes did not leave his after the smile. Beneath the face-down phone, {name} felt the numbers fall quiet.

choices.text: Admit what he was calculating. "The truth is, I'm scared."
choices.result_text:
"About money?"
"About ruining everything. What I have now, and whatever I might have later."

Daeun did not rush to tell him it would be fine. She wrapped both hands around the cold cup instead. "Does a day ever come when everything is ready?"

{name} had no answer. Daeun listened even to that silence.

title: This Time Next Year
description:
The ice in their cups had nearly melted. One of the lights above the counter went dark, and the remaining customers began to leave.

"Minjun."
"Yes?"
"What I said about next year — I meant it."

Daeun did not press him. She did not look like someone trying to force an answer. She simply stayed, as she had for four years, while {name} searched for the words.

Daeun put a hand on the strap of her bag. If she stood now, tonight would end like any other night.

choices.text: Call to her before she stands. "Wait."
choices.result_text:
Daeun's hand stopped on the strap.

"Yes, Minjun?"

She sat back down. This time, the corner of the box did not slip away from his fingertips.

title: The Proposal
description:
Daeun sat down again. The sounds of the cafe seemed to take one step back from the table.

{name}'s thumb pressed against the corner of the box in his pocket. He had hesitated for days. The price of a ring could have been seed money — and for the first time, doing that math made him ashamed.

Across from him sat the person who had endured four years in this cramped city beside him. Whether he reached Gangnam or not, she had stayed.

Daeun waited. Not rushing him, simply looking at him.

This was the moment.

choices.text: Take out the box. "I haven't reached Gangnam yet — but I want to make this promise first."
choices.result_text:
The box opened on the table. Daeun's gaze stopped on the ring. She drew one breath and found no words.

Her hand flew to her mouth. Her eyes reddened in an instant.
"...Idiot. How many times do I have to tell you? Gangnam doesn't matter."
"That's why I'm asking. Even without Gangnam, you were enough for me."

Daeun nodded hard, over and over.

The woman who had handed him a rice ball at a convenience store five years ago was now the person he had promised his life to.
Five years that couldn't be counted in numbers, all fit into one ring on one finger.

choices.text: Put the box away. "Just a little more... when I'm ready." (Not yet)
choices.result_text:
The box spent another night in his pocket.

Daeun seemed to notice, or maybe not.
"Were you going to say something?"
"...No. Let's eat."

When he was ready. Even {name} could not say what 'ready' meant.
Whether Gangnam came first, or she did — he had postponed the answer again.

description_if_known.daeun_first_night:

He remembered that rainy night: the hand that turned off the light, the narrow bed in the morning. Perhaps he had already known then that she was the one.

Daeun waited. Not rushing him, simply looking at him.

This was the moment.
description_if_known.daeun_seen_by_gifts:
Daeun sat down again. The sounds of the cafe seemed to take one step back from the table.

{name}'s thumb pressed against the corner of the box in his pocket. He had hesitated for days. The price of a ring could have been seed money — and for the first time, doing that math made him ashamed.

Canned coffee, socks, a scarf. Things that cost very little, yet Daeun had smiled for so long each time. He had never given her anything expensive. Instead, each time, he had truly seen her.

Daeun waited. Not rushing him, simply looking at him.

This was the moment.
